**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 92, verses 14–21:**

﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes fiercely.﴾ *Tatawwaqadu* (تتوقد) means it blazes and flares up. ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read *tatalaẓẓā* (تتلظى) in its original form, while others read it with the letter deleted. ﴿None will enter it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away.﴾

Abu Hurayra recited: "He will surely enter Paradise, except whoever refuses (*yaʾbā*)." They said: "O Abu Hurayra, and who would refuse to enter Paradise?" He then recited His saying, ﴿who denied and turned away.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Burhan ibn ʿAli al-Sufi told us, saying: Abu Khalifa told us, saying: al-Qaʿnabi told us, saying: Malik told us, saying: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Aziz led us in the Maghrib prayer, and he recited in it ﴿By the night when it covers﴾. When he reached this verse, ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes fiercely,﴾ weeping overcame him, and he could not get past it because of his weeping. Then he recited another surah.

﴿And the most righteous will be spared it, the one who gives his wealth to purify himself.﴾ The scholars of meanings (*ahl al-maʿani*) said: He intended "the wretched" and "the righteous," as in the verse of Tarafa:

*They wished that men would die; if I die, that is a path in which I am not unique.*

That is, "not one alone."
